review_outline.summary: The paper defines the Belief-Claim Gap, estimates it by active black-box tomography with Wilson intervals and a certification semantics, proves an impossibility result, a query-complexity bound, a deception-detection frontier, and a set of certification limits, and reports thirty registered experiments on constructed foils, a commercial gateway lane, a live honeypot fleet, and three open-weight models. Both pre-registered field predictions were refuted at instrument resolution, and the program caught two of its own measurement errors. Round 18 reviewed the IEEE TDSC build with five independent seats (theory re-derivation, empirical recount, gatekeeping, fresh-eyes craft, consistency) and applied every verified correction.

strengths.text: The empirical program survives a full recount: 33 Wilson/Clopper-Pearson intervals recompute to the digit from frozen artifacts, the 230-flag audit decomposes exactly (118 refusal-quote false positives, 112 genuine canary echoes), the censoring counters (591 + 83 + 305 = 979) and every table cell in the field, open-weight, and audit tables match the raw verdicts. The two self-caught errors are real and correctly attributed.

The theory is now sound at the points where it was weakest. The onset theorem's certified horizon uses the exact two-sample variance, is finite exactly when the shift exceeds the certified boundary, and reproduces M*=29.73 at the registered cell; the exact binomial test's power is corrected to 0.785 at (40,0.2); the certification rule's Wilson trichotomy is respected by Proposition 6 and E13; and the sensitivity statement is correctly presented as an identity for binary verdicts rather than an assumption test.

The honesty layer is unusually complete and now matches the record: the registration ledger distinguishes clean, same-commit, with-data, and post-data entries experiment by experiment (per-experiment timing in Supplement Table S2), discloses the two header-date edits, withdraws the earlier universal pre-registration phrasing, reports both field predictions as refuted, and states the 24/6 confirmatory-exploratory split as retroactive.

weaknesses.text: The bibliography is still ACM-Reference-Format in an IEEE submission: full given names, year after authors, quoted titles, 'In Proceedings of', and only a third of entries carrying DOIs. Ordering is alphabetical rather than first-citation. An IEEE production editor will return it; converting 43 entries to IEEE punctuation with volumes, pages, and DOIs is the remaining production task.

Fitting the 12-page Transactions limit cost the main paper every figure: the tomogram, the onset grid, the certification attack surface, and the release wave now live only in the supplement, and the main text is figure-free. A 13-page paper with one figure (0.5 page over the current fit) would read better, and the figure set would need regeneration at column width with Type 1 fonts before submission.

The field panel is thin by construction: one model per gateway lane at the deployed depth, with censoring that leaves the primary lane's state-deception family unidentified ([0,1]) in E2-v1. The paper says this, and the repaired panel and the open-weight models mitigate it, but a reviewer will still ask for a second lane at the repaired budget.

The deposit's own record includes post-data registrations in the E20-E29 window. This is disclosed rather than repaired, which is the honest treatment, but it means the exploratory diagnostics cannot be read as confirmatory even where their results are clean.
